summary:
Set 127 Session 2 puts the missing middle frame on the operator's screen. Session 1 derived two facts in the Python row model -- which step a session is currently on, and when each started row started -- from rows both surfaces already read. This session mirrors that derivation in TypeScript, pins the two implementations against each other, and renders the result in the Work Explorer, so the surface the defect was reported against now answers the question that opened the note.

(1) THE MIRROR, AND EVERY CONSUMER OF A ROW STATUS. `providers/sessionStepModel.ts` gains `sessionFlightFacts`, `activeStepIndex`, `deriveProgress`, `effectiveStatusOf`, a `RowEvidence` type and two new `StepRow` fields; `reconcile` now returns evidence so the start time is derived in the same pass, exactly as `_reconcile` does in Python. The one deliberate difference is that `sessionFlightFacts` takes an already-parsed state object rather than reading the file -- this module has no `fs` import by design and the scan has the state in hand. Step 2's real requirement was NOT the derivation but the echo pass (L-069-1): `stepDescriptor` has TWO consumers of a row's status, and the tooltip's planned branch would otherwise have called the running step 'planned -- not started' in prose while the icon beside it showed it running. Both now read `effectiveStatusOf`, and a `step-active` contextValue token is minted so a `when` clause can distinguish 'planned' from 'planned AND in flight'.

(2) THE START TIME, RENDERED WHERE A WORSE ANSWER USED TO LIVE. Each started row shows `12:06-` in VS Code's dimmed description slot -- the slot the `<- here` marker occupied until Set 115 S4 retired it, so nothing is displaced. Local, 24-hour, hour and minute, trailing dash to mark it a start rather than a completion; the full timestamp goes in the tooltip where width is free. A row that has not started renders no description at all, which is what stops a seeded row's REGISTRATION stamp being shown as a start (operator ruling 3). An unparseable timestamp also renders nothing, unlike the neighbouring `asOfLabel`, because this slot is a few characters wide beside a label.

(3) THE CROSS-LANGUAGE WINDOW SESSION 1 OPENED IS CLOSED. The parity corpus grew from 14 cases to 23 and now models the two inputs the derivation needs -- a per-case `sessionState` and per-entry `dateTime` -- so `DERIVED_ROW_FIELDS` is gone and all seven row fields are compared in both languages again. Eight of the nine new cases pin the derivation in both directions by name (fires: silent record, skipped step, prose status; does not fire: closed session, blocked row, a logged in-progress row above a pending planned one, no state file at all), and BOTH halves independently assert the corpus still carries them, so neither language owns the gate. Both halves also re-run every case a second time with the state file withheld, which falsifies 'derives on a session nobody said was in flight' across the whole corpus rather than on the one case written for it.

(4) FALSIFIERS PROVEN TO BITE. Eight defects were planted against the finished suite and every one was caught: dropping the record-wins guard (4 failures), ignoring the in-flight gate (18), reading eligibility through TypeScript's not-started FALLBACK instead of the token table (2), marking every eligible planned row (5), treating a bookkeeping record as a step in the start-time chain (1), rendering the glyph from the raw record (2), letting the tooltip's planned branch answer first (1), and showing a time on a row that has not started (5). The harness refused to score a mutation that failed to compile, and was deleted after it ran. Six of the eight were two lines or fewer, which is the evidence behind this session's recommendation against a line-count-based verification carve-out.

(5) THE UAT WALK IS RUNNABLE, NOT JUST WRITTEN. `s2-uat-walk.md` is one Look item and two Decide items sourced from the journalled operator rulings. The uat-matrix fixture it runs on could not have shown the feature -- its in-flight session carried no seeded plan, a shape no real set has had since Set 114 S2 -- so the fixture was given one, and its rendered rows (done + 11:00-, DERIVED in-progress + 11:30-, unstarted + no time) are now pinned by a Layer 2 test through the real scan. project-guidance's rule is that everything automation can check is checked before the human is asked; an unrunnable walk fails that on the first line.

VERIFICATION: round 1 discovery (fan-out 2, spec-conformance + failure-scenario, both gpt-5.5) returned ONE Major and it was this session's own defect: `readSessionSets` infers an in-memory `in-progress` state when `session-state.json` is absent -- a supported path -- and this session wired that inferred object into `sessionFlightFacts`, so the tree would have derived an active step and start times where Python (`read_session_state` -> None) derives neither. Broader than reported: the start-time half needs no seeded plan to diverge, and the inferred `startedAt` is the log's EARLIEST entry, a different quantity from a session start. Round 2 supplementary found nothing new. Fixed by arming the derivation only from a state file really on disk (`normalizedState = stateFileOnDisk ? sd : null`), with the inference still driving bucketing and row rendering exactly as before; the new falsifier fails pre-fix with `inFlight: true` and passes post-fix, run rather than asserted. Round 3 remediation-review: VERIFIED, fix accepted, 0 findings.

PROCESS DEFECT, RECORDED NOT BURIED: this session ran its full pytest and Playwright suites BEFORE verification, which is the wrong order -- the constitution puts full suites after verification and remediation precisely so a remediation does not stale them. It did, and both were re-run after the fix (pytest stayed fresh; mocha and Playwright were re-run and re-recorded). The cause was this session's own spec compressing 'full suites; verify; close' into one step in the wrong internal order, which Session 1's spec got right. Cause, cost and a proposed structural fix -- a fixed step skeleton enforced by `spec_admission`, plus the ordering rules -- are captured in `docs/planning/session-step-skeleton-and-verification-cost.md` for its own future set. It is deliberately NOT bolted onto Session 3.

reason.specifics: Session 3 is the set-terminal session and its subject -- making the verification-round boundary post its own checklist -- is the third surface answering the same question this session just answered on the second. It also inherits three things authored here that need continuity rather than rediscovery: the s2-uat-walk.md this set's per-set UAT obligation will point at, the settled by-design ruling on the start-time chain, and the process-defect note in docs/planning/. No capability, cost or context pressure argues for a switch; cross-provider independence is supplied by verification, which excluded anthropic on all three rounds.
